intro.text:
The tables below define the display, labelling, and behavioural requirements for the Insurance Data Sharing
 consents in the LFI Consent Management Interface (CMI). See the User Experience
 page for interactive wireframes of the dashboard and detail pages.

The LFI CMI shares the same structure and consent-type logic as the TPP CMI for Insurance Data Sharing
, with the differences noted below. Adjustments to the requirements below are permitted provided the customer can always clearly understand what consents they have granted. Any adjustments must be documented in your CX certification submission.

blocks.text:
Paused
 is not a valid status in the LFI CMI. It is a TPP-local concept that is not reflected in the API Hub.
The dashboard must present Insurance Data Sharing consents across two tabs.

rows:
The Current
 tab must display all consents whose status is AwaitingAuthorization
, Authorized
, or Suspended
.

The History
 tab must display all consents whose status is Rejected
, Expired
, or Revoked
.

blocks.text: A filter panel must be available on the dashboard. The following three filters are required:

rows: Dynamically populated from the TPPs present in the customer's connections
Dynamically populated from the types present in the current tab
Dynamically populated from the statuses present in the current tab

blocks.text: Consent statuses must be translated from their API values into user-friendly labels before display.
Each Insurance Data Sharing consent card on the dashboard must show the following fields.

rows: Name of the TPP the consent was granted to

Number of connected policies, e.g. 1 Policy Connected
 or 2 Policies Connected
Date the most recent data was retrieved under this consent

blocks.text:
Selecting a consent on the dashboard opens its detail page. The detail page presents the same information the customer saw at the time they gave consent — the permissions, policies, and conditions that defined what they agreed to. In addition to all fields shown on the dashboard card, the detail page must show a truncated Consent ID with a copy button (format: f47ac10b...d479
).

rows:
List of all insurance policies the customer has connected under this consent, each showing the policy type (e.g. Motor
, Health
, Life
), the insurer, and the policy number

Expandable list of data categories the consent covers, derived from the consent's Permissions
 field — e.g. Policy details
, Premium details
, Claim details

blocks.text: The LFI CMI does not include Pause or Reactivate buttons. These are TPP-only concepts.

rows:
Status is AwaitingAuthorization
, Authorized
, or Suspended

blocks.text:
No action buttons are shown when status is Expired
, Rejected
, or Revoked
.

When the customer selects Revoke, replace the detail view with a single confirmation screen
 that includes: a title, a description of the impact of the action on the service, a Confirm button, and a Go back button.

Once a customer confirms the action, the change must take effect immediately — there must be no delay between confirmation and the consent reflecting its new state. The LFI must update the consent status via the Consent Manager API.
